best_for: Developers and tinkerers with a recent NVIDIA or AMD card, or an Apple silicon Mac, who want to run open-weight language models locally and call them from their own scripts.

points.title: Local use is free
points.text: Ollama is MIT licensed, and running models on your own hardware is free with no usage cap. Cloud models are optional: pay as you go, Pro at USD 20 a month or 200 a year with USD 60 of monthly credits, or Max at USD 100 a month with USD 300. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Plan for disk space
points.text: The app needs about 4 GB, and models can take tens to hundreds of GB. Set `OLLAMA_MODELS` to keep them on a bigger drive.

points.title: What Windows needs
points.text: Windows 10 22H2 or newer. NVIDIA cards need driver 551.61 or later; AMD cards use ROCm v7 or Vulkan. The installer puts Ollama in your home folder without administrator rights, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Intel Macs run on CPU
points.text: The Mac app needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later. Apple silicon Macs use both CPU and GPU, while Intel Macs run models on the CPU only, which is much slower.

points.title: A local API for your code
points.text: Ollama serves an HTTP API on `localhost:11434` and includes the `ollama` command. On a Mac the app offers to link the command into `/usr/local/bin` on first launch.

points.title: Updates and older versions
points.text: The Mac and Windows apps download updates and ask you to restart. The Windows listing keeps 212 versions; macOS lists only the current release. Linux is not listed here; Ollama installs there with its own script.
